provenance.notes: Numerical observations copied from the private pen capture records (background constraint cells C1-C3, D; K-B2 B5-B7b) and K-C2 (C2h, C2i); the private findings remain the source of record.

_about: The polygon pen over a BACKGROUND surface with the surface constraint on (geometry off unless swept, snapping off unless stated). Background: a sphere of radius 1, 64 sides x 32 segments, centre (0,1,0) unless stated, in a background layer; the foreground mesh starts empty. Top orthographic view, 440 px per metre, focus (0.07, 1, 0): the click quantum is 0.005 and every click aims at a lattice point, so x/z are exact. A point lands on the background hit on the view ray through its quantised plane point (the first point = the create click, a later one = the plane through the current point, a drag = the plane through the dragged point); the constraint's `handle` flag gates it, its geometry mode does not; a miss keeps the plane point; the offset moves the hit along the hit normal after the quantum; a vertex snap replaces all three channels and the pen welds onto the snapped vertex; a typed position stands. Heights are the reference's depth read (1/1024 lattice, 1.1-1.6e-3 below the facets): tolerance 2e-3.

C1.law: handle on: the surface on the vertical ray through q, identical for every geometry mode; handle off or the constraint off: the plane (y 1)

C2b.law: a miss after a hit lands on the plane through the previous point, its normal channel quantised (1.93, not 1.930664)

C3.law: the constraint applies while dragging a placed point

D.law: mirror points are exact reflections of the constrained originals, not re-projected (independent projections 1.686 / miss / 1.625)

B7.law: constrained click x/z are quantised like plane clicks; a typed position stands (no re-projection: 1.8691)

B7b.tol_note: p3 (0.8, 0) lies on a longitude edge of the sphere (z 0): ours offsets along ONE facet's normal (2.3 deg off the radial, measured 2026-10-05: z 0.003943), the record's depth-read normal averages across the edge (z -0.000977); 4.9e-3 apart. The offset-after-quantum law is held by the length / direction asserts, not by this compare
B7b.law: the offset moves the surface hit 0.1 along the hit normal after the quantum (the reference normal is a depth-read normal 1-2 deg off the facet: every channel carries up to offset * sin(2 deg) = 3.5e-3)

B6.height_tol_note: this cell's depth reads sit lower: ours (facet hits) minus the record measured +2.7e-3 (p0) and +2.0e-3 (p2) on 2026-10-05; the guide's pull it guards against moves p3 by >= 5e-3 in z (onto z 0) or 0.18 in y
B6.law: with the background constraint on, a dragged point lands on the surface under the cursor (x/z quantised); the straight-line guide (the line z 0 through p1, p2; it engages at 5.8 px without the background) does not pull it onto the 3D line (y 2.1595) nor onto the line's surface projection (z 0)

C2i.more_clicks_note: rig completion (a polygon needs three points): two clicks off the sphere, away from every vertex
C2i.law: SNAP-LAST: a foreground vertex in range replaces all three channels of the surface point; the pen's polygon reuses it (nv 3), unlike the vertex tool (nv 2)

C2h.law: the pen's first point equals the vertex tool's at the same pixel (1e-6, both oblique ortho rigs and the persp rig)
